messages:
deploy-bot: Canary rollout `release/optimize-routing` started in prod(us-west-2) — 10% traffic, 3 replicas. rollout_id=rl_2026_03_15_01

maria (oncall): noticing a spike in 5xx on canary hostpool within last 2m, healthcheck flapping on /healthz :
- 200 -> 503 -> 200 -> 503 repeated

jacob (sre): confirmed, seeing increased p95 latency to ~2.1s and a bunch of 503s. autoscaler not implicated yet.

incident-bot: Paging oncall: maria — high-error-rate detected for service inference-api (canary). Incident created: INC-20260315-01.

maria (oncall): acked. @sam can you pull logs for canary pods? tagging in case routing/compile changes in this release. :eyes:

sam (prod-eng): on it. pulling pod logs — seeing repeated timeouts to model backend: 
```
2026-03-15T01:12:23Z inference: request id=abc123 status=upstream_timeout backend=rt-infer-02 latency=3000ms
2026-03-15T01:12:24Z healthcheck: probe failed, code=503 reason="upstream timeout"
```

bethany (support): any customer-facing impact yet? Support reports 4 user errors from integrations in last 3m. Possibly increased error pages for streaming endpoints.

maria (oncall): impact appears limited but growing. For safety we should hit abort criteria: >0.5% 5xx across 10m or repeated health probe failures on canary. Current short-window breach observed. Recommending temporary kill-switch on feature flag `optimize-routing.canary` and rollback to previous model variant.

jacob (sre): agree. Can we toggle the flag quickly? ops-bot, can you run the kill-switch?

ops-bot: Executing: `ffctl set optimize-routing.canary off --reason "canary health failures" --by maria`
ops-bot: Flag updated. New state: optimize-routing.canary = OFF

deploy-bot: Canary rollout paused and traffic re-routed to stable pool. Notifying autoscale that canary replicas should be drained.

sam (prod-eng): initiating graceful drain of canary pods and triggering rollback pipeline: `ci rollback --to=rl_stable_20260310`

maria (oncall): monitoring metrics — p95 latency and 5xx count dropping on next 60s window. Good sign.

jacob (sre): digging into root cause — early hypothesis: connection pool exhaustion when fallback routing increases backend calls per-request. There's a concurrent-change in routing logic that increases backend fanout for some prompt types.

sam (prod-eng): I see a regression in routing config: `fanout=3` for certain long prompts was introduced in this release. Reverting config change locally reproduced the 503 pattern.

bethany (support): logged incident note for customers impacted and created a triage item to contact any paying customers who hit errors > 5 requests.

maria (oncall): incident severity set to sev2. No broad outage; customer impact limited to a small fraction of traffic. Current action items: 1) rollback complete 2) verify healthchecks stable 3) run canary with smaller surface (split by route) after fix 4) postmortem + rollout checklist update.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20260315-01 status: mitigated. Pager cleared at 01:18 UTC.

jacob (sre): performing post-handoff checks, leaving notes for next oncall: root cause = routing fanout change leading to backend saturation on certain prompt shapes; mitigation = flag kill + rollback; follow-ups = adjust default fanout, add circuit-breaker on backend calls, add canary test for high-fanout routes.

maria (oncall): handing off to @night-oncall (tom) — summary: rolled back rl_2026_03_15_01 after health checks failed, customers limited impact, follow-ups assigned to prod-eng (sam) and SRE (jacob). See INC-20260315-01 for links/logs.

sam (prod-eng): will own the fix. plan to add a small synthetic test exercising long prompts to catch fanout regressions in future canaries.

bethany (support): will notify any affected customers with timeline and mitigation steps.

maria (oncall): closing thread, leaving monitoring for 30m. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
